title: Yep. Sorry Bill. I will take some responsibility, but it was inevitable. When Twitter first started, I started posting press conference quotes on BLACKBERRY LOL, tweeting camp updates. Wasn't common. Then when everybody did it, I stopped because it was expected, being handled and then some. I will also take credit/blame for being one of the people trying to get @MarkBerman_ to tweet instead of others just quoting and linking to his scoops. Early years of social were kinda weird and wild for sports media. Some of the press guidelines we see now come from odd things that happened then. Same thing goes for gameday rules. Like when you see a weird rule, it means that something weird happened, so they created a rule, like with the balloon thing that caused a power outage. Ultimately, it's just better for everybody to be Texas neighborly, understand each others' wants and needs, than it is to be sticklers for rules. Anyway, I love the sports media folks posting their things. That is really hard to do well, anyone who thinks differently, likely hasn't done it.

Yep. Sorry Bill. I will take some responsibility, but it was inevitable. When Twitter first started, I started posting press conference quotes on BLACKBERRY LOL, tweeting camp updates. Wasn't common. 

Then when everybody did it, I stopped because it was expected, being handled and then some.

I will also take credit/blame for being one of the people trying to get @MarkBerman_ to tweet instead of others just quoting and linking to his scoops. 

Early years of social were kinda weird and wild for sports media. Some of the press guidelines we see now come from odd things that happened then. 

Same thing goes for gameday rules. Like when you see a weird rule, it means that something weird happened, so they created a rule, like with the balloon thing that caused a power outage. 

Ultimately, it's just better for everybody to be Texas neighborly, understand each others' wants and needs, than it is to be sticklers for rules. 

Anyway, I love the sports media folks posting their things. That is really hard to do well, anyone who thinks differently, likely hasn't done it.

title: Practice report: • Lot of short passes from Jaxson Dart today while they were drilling a lot of third/fourth and short/medium ... until the final period. The offense was trailing by 14 points with 7:55 remaining in the fourth quarter in the situation. That provided a learning opportunity for rookie corner Colton Hood, who bit on a pump fake and allowed Darius Slayton to get open behind him for a long touchdown. • The second-team offense's drive came to an end when rookie RB Damon Bankston fumbled on fourth-and-1 and DL Marlon Davidson recovered. • The third-team offense's drive came to a premature end after Jalin Hyatt's right ankle was rolled up by LB Darius Muasua's diving tackle attempt. Harbaugh said Hyatt seemed to be OK, but will undergo further examination. Harbaugh (and every coach) doesn't want players laying out for tackles to avoid those types of collisions. • Patrick Ricard and Arvell Reese are the hammers on each side of the ball. They met with a violent collision in a 9-on-7 drill today that Ricard got the better of. • Hood, Paulson Adebo and Deonte Banks had a three-way rotation with the two outside corner spots on the first-team defense with Greg Newsome sidelined by a knee injury that Harbaugh indicated is minor. Adebo intercepted an under-thrown fade from Jameis Winston while playing with the first-team defense against the second-team offense. Winston responded with a perfect deep pass up the seam to tight end Thomas Fidone, who made a tough catch between Hood and Jevon Holland. Fidone's hands have really flashed lately. He garnered a low five from Harbaugh after snagging a bullet from Winston in a 7-on-7 period in Saturday's practice. • There was more mixing and matching with the backup offensive lines today. Rookie JC Davis got all of the second-team reps at LT for the first time with Marcus Mbow kicking over to RT. Josh Ezeudu slid into RG after spending the first 10 practices exclusively at RT. Aaron Stinnie and Daniel Faalele alternated at LG with Jake Kubas stepping at center.

title: Nick Sirianni on his team speech with the team slogan of 100% alignment, 0 entitlement. And Nick mentioned the book to his players, Chop Wood, Carry Water ”What resonated with me the most is that there is no secret to why success happens. It's really hard, dirty work at the end of the day. I can resonate with that. It's hard, dirty work at the end of the day that's going to get it done. Sometimes we can get caught up in the flash of whatever, but at the end of the day, tackling wins. At the end of the day, block destruction wins. At the end of the day, toughness wins. At the end of the day, ball security and takeaway ability wins. At the end of the day, blocking wins. So all these fundamentals that can get overlooked sometimes are what makes it happen. The only way to get better at those fundamentals, It's not going to happen just because you're talented. It's going to happen because of the work that you put in. I can just resonate with that so much. So many of our guys on the team can resonate with that so much. We know that if we put the work in on a daily basis, we can, God willing, reach where we need to go as a football team and be playing our best football by the end of the year. You've got our leaders on the football team that guys are constantly looking at to see how they're working. I think that we have a bunch of guys like that on this team. One thing that is very obvious is that our best players work the hardest and you'll be exposed if you don't. Alignment is so critical. We all have to understand this. That's not only alignment within the coaching staff, that's alignment from coaching staff to players. Since day one here, I feel like we've had great alignment there and how they relay the message. You can relay the message as much as you want, but everybody's looking at your actions. So, at the end of the day, am I living the tough, detailed, together-world? Are our leaders on our football team living the tough, detailed, together-world? Is that trickling down to everybody else because the coaching staff and the leaders on the football team are doing that?”

title: Schedule Update and league talk: I'm told CB Terrion Arnold's visit with the #Saints is Tuesday. Visits in Indy or Baltimore are not imminently expected, at this time, per league sources. As for Arnold's visit in Seattle I was told, "seems like a good kid and like he wants another chance. We'll see what happens." title: Notes and observations from #49ers practice No. 10: - RB Christian McCaffrey was the only addition to the not practicing report Monday with what the team called "tightness." Understandably, lots of eyes will be on that situation. OC Klay Kubiak says the team is "just managing" McCaffrey with an eye toward having him ready for Week 1 against the Rams. We'll see if he's in the mix for a joint practice tomorrow but (my take) seems more likely they'd hold him out so he can get this week to rid himself of that tightness. He'd be unlikely to play Thursday night anyway. - Coach Kyle Shanahan was out there for essentially the entire practice as he continues his road back to full strength. - One notable thing from before practice: TE George Kittle did the most extensive side work we've been able to see so far in this camp. He was running routes, catching passes and doing some conditioning. Seems to be moving quite well as he bounces back from Achilles injury. - The full list of those missing practice today: McCaffrey, LB Luke Gifford (hamstring), DE Nick Bosa (soreness), WR Jacob Cowing (hip flexor strain), FB Kyle Juszczyk (broken finger), OL Brett Toth (concussion), WR Christian Kirk (calf), WR Mike Evans (quad), S Malik Mustapha (hamstring), RB Kaelon Black (adductor), RB Jordan James (rib), DL Keion White (adductor), OT Vederian Lowe (ankle) Players on PUP: Kittle (achilles), RB Isaac Guerendo (pec), DL Mykel Williams (ACL) - Almost all of those guys did at least some level of work on the side during practice. That included Evans, of course, but this is first time I've seen White and Black doing stuff since their adductor injuries. - OL Carver Willis is back from his concussion. He jumped right in with the 2s at LG with Connor Colby on the right side. Robert Jones continues to rep with the 1s at LG. Kubiak says the competition for the starting LG spot is still open. - A roster move: Team released OL Nick Zakelj. They signed OL Doug Kramer Jr. - A number change: WR Will Pauling switched from No. 4 to No. 84. He and QB Adrian Martinez were both in 4 but changed presumably because they need to have different numbers for the preseason game when they might be on the field at the same time. - Some pretty good battles in one-on-one pass rush drills today. Not a lot of convincing wins on either side, which means it was pretty good work. Among the standouts: Colton McKivitz doing well against Sam Okauyinonu followed by a good battle with Romello Height in which McKivitz seemed to have him stopped but Height spun out of it for a late pressure... It's been a rough camp for Enrique Cruz Jr. but he had a nice recovery on an outside rush from Ogbo Okoronkwo, though K.J. Henry later beat him cleanly... C.J. West had a good rep early against C Jake Brendel though he and Brendel later had another good battle... In one sequence, Willis took back to back reps, one at C and one at LG. He was beat clean at center by West then moved to guard and did very well against Osa Odighizuwa. Suffice to say, Willis a work in progress at C and looks more comfortable at G, as you'd expect... The Niners worked TE Luke Farrell in a bit here, isolating him against DEs Titus Leo and Quinton Bell. Leo and Bell got the better of him, though Farrell put up a fight in both. - Another solid day with some big plays for QB Brock Purdy and the offense. I had Purdy at 10-of-13 (would-be sacks and some penalties nullified a few throws to my eye). He hit rookie WR De'Zhaun Stribling on a perfect deep corner for a huge gain and later found WR Demarcus Robinson for another big play/would-be TD. Purdy also hit Deebo over the middle for what would have been a big gainer. - One of those stops on Purdy I had as a would-be sack for LB Fred Warner. Purdy scrambled away from pressure but Warner came up and made the play. Warner also had a big thud on WR Junior Bergen after he caught a short pass. - With their projected top four RBs not practicing, there was plenty of work for the others on the roster today, perhaps most notably Khalil Herbert. Wouldn't be surprised if Herbert gets plenty of work on Thursday night along with Patrick Taylor Jr. and Sincere McCormick. - CB Jack Jones had another interception, this time jumping in front of a throw from Martinez for WR Jordan Watkins. - A couple of drops Monday as Samuel had a Purdy pass go through his hands and bounce off his chest and McCormick failed to haul in another throw from Purdy. - LB Nick Martin had a nice run stuff while playing on the LOS and DT Sebastian Valdez had a would-be sack. - A relatively light session though with plenty of team periods and some competitive move the ball and red zone sessions. Things will pick up a bit more tomorrow when the Titans come to town for a joint practice. Will have plenty from that. Thanks for reading.

title: Brock Purdy is now the only remaining player from the 49ers' 2022 draft class. SF released Nick Zakelj to make room for center Doug Kramer Jr. before practice. Some highlights... 🏈Purdy's explosive camp continues. Deep 70-yard TDs to both De'Zhaun Stribling and Demarcus Robinson 🏈George Kittle looks to be truly ramping it up. Was moving and cutting well in what looked to be some aggressive rehab work 🏈Mike Evans and Christian Kirk both look like they might be close to returning. Shanahan essentially said Evans' absence is precautionary 🏈Brett Toth (concussion) was on an exercise bike. Might he be a dark horse to grab the LG spot? It's Robert Jones - Connor Colby there right now, but Klay Kubiak said it's "still an open competition" and, with Kramer added, the 49ers now have more center depth 🏈Safety Marques Sigle says he's gained 8-10 pounds of muscle since last season. Thinks it'll allow him to be more physical while keeping his 4.37 speed. Robinson did beat Sigle, though, on the second long Purdy TD toss 🏈Rookie Carver Willis cleared concussion protocol and was back at practice. He's getting work at both guard spots and center 🏈Big hit from Fred Warner on WR Junior Bergen — but to Bergen's credit, he held onto the football. He's been tough all camp 🏈Deebo Samuel worked a bit in the RB room today. Shifted back to the WRs to close position group drills. Caught a nice seam shot in stride and dropped an out while working against Dre Greenlaw 🏈Sigle on Greenlaw: "His energy never left. He stayed in this room even though he wasn’t here.” 🏈Looked like officials called PI against rookie CB Ephesians Prysock on a deep out from Mac Jones to Demarcus Robinson. Prysock was flagged a few times at UW last year; definitely a clean-up spot 🏈Romello Height has a tendency to jump offside in 1-on-1s. Clearly trying to buy an advantage for his lighter frame, but it'll be a mandatory part of his game to iron out 🏈Best 1-on-1 recovery rep from rookie OT Enrique Cruz Jr. so far. Ogbo Okoronkwo beat him off the snap but Cruz did well to readjust. Raw prospect, but some progress is evident 🏈Colby had really struggled in 1-on-1s as of late, but worth noting that he had a solid win today vs DT CJ West. Sweet rep ft. a spin move from Sam Okuayinonu vs Colton McKivitz, too — Colton later shut down Height 🏈CMC's absence Monday was essentially precautionary, per Kubiak. Joint practice against Saleh and the Titans tomorrow — we'll see if McCaffrey is back out there
summary:
Brock Purdy is now the only remaining player from the 49ers' 2022 draft class. SF released Nick Zakelj to make room for center Doug Kramer Jr. before practice. Some highlights...

🏈Purdy's explosive camp continues. Deep 70-yard TDs to both De'Zhaun Stribling and Demarcus Robinson
🏈George Kittle looks to be truly ramping it up. Was moving and cutting well in what looked to be some aggressive rehab work
🏈Mike Evans and Christian Kirk both look like they might be close to returning. Shanahan essentially said Evans' absence is precautionary
🏈Brett Toth (concussion) was on an exercise bike. Might he be a dark horse to grab the LG spot? It's Robert Jones - Connor Colby there right now, but Klay Kubiak said it's "still an open competition" and, with Kramer added, the 49ers now have more center depth
🏈Safety Marques Sigle says he's gained 8-10 pounds of muscle since last season. Thinks it'll allow him to be more physical while keeping his 4.37 speed. Robinson did beat Sigle, though, on the second long Purdy TD toss
🏈Rookie Carver Willis cleared concussion protocol and was back at practice. He's getting work at both guard spots and center
🏈Big hit from Fred Warner on WR Junior Bergen — but to Bergen's credit, he held onto the football. He's been tough all camp
🏈Deebo Samuel worked a bit in the RB room today. Shifted back to the WRs to close position group drills. Caught a nice seam shot in stride and dropped an out while working against Dre Greenlaw 
🏈Sigle on Greenlaw: "His energy never left. He stayed in this room even though he wasn’t here.”
🏈Looked like officials called PI against rookie CB Ephesians Prysock on a deep out from Mac Jones to Demarcus Robinson. Prysock was flagged a few times at UW last year; definitely a clean-up spot
🏈Romello Height has a tendency to jump offside in 1-on-1s. Clearly trying to buy an advantage for his lighter frame, but it'll be a mandatory part of his game to iron out
🏈Best 1-on-1 recovery rep from rookie OT Enrique Cruz Jr. so far. Ogbo Okoronkwo beat him off the snap but Cruz did well to readjust. Raw prospect, but some progress is evident
🏈Colby had really struggled in 1-on-1s as of late, but worth noting that he had a solid win today vs DT CJ West. Sweet rep ft. a spin move from Sam Okuayinonu vs Colton McKivitz, too — Colton later shut down Height
🏈CMC's absence Monday was essentially precautionary, per Kubiak. Joint practice against Saleh and the Titans tomorrow — we'll see if McCaffrey is back out there

Brock Purdy is now the only remaining player from the 49ers' 2022 draft class. SF released Nick Zakelj to make room for center Doug Kramer Jr. before practice. Some highlights...

🏈Purdy's explosive camp continues. Deep 70-yard TDs to both De'Zhaun Stribling and Demarcus Robinson
🏈George Kittle looks to be truly ramping it up. Was moving and cutting well in what looked to be some aggressive rehab work
🏈Mike Evans and Christian Kirk both look like they might be close to returning. Shanahan essentially said Evans' absence is precautionary
🏈Brett Toth (concussion) was on an exercise bike. Might he be a dark horse to grab the LG spot? It's Robert Jones - Connor Colby there right now, but Klay Kubiak said it's "still an open competition" and, with Kramer added, the 49ers now have more center depth
🏈Safety Marques Sigle says he's gained 8-10 pounds of muscle since last season. Thinks it'll allow him to be more physical while keeping his 4.37 speed. Robinson did beat Sigle, though, on the second long Purdy TD toss
🏈Rookie Carver Willis cleared concussion protocol and was back at practice. He's getting work at both guard spots and center
🏈Big hit from Fred Warner on WR Junior Bergen — but to Bergen's credit, he held onto the football. He's been tough all camp
🏈Deebo Samuel worked a bit in the RB room today. Shifted back to the WRs to close position group drills. Caught a nice seam shot in stride and dropped an out while working against Dre Greenlaw 
🏈Sigle on Greenlaw: "His energy never left. He stayed in this room even though he wasn’t here.”
🏈Looked like officials called PI against rookie CB Ephesians Prysock on a deep out from Mac Jones to Demarcus Robinson. Prysock was flagged a few times at UW last year; definitely a clean-up spot
🏈Romello Height has a tendency to jump offside in 1-on-1s. Clearly trying to buy an advantage for his lighter frame, but it'll be a mandatory part of his game to iron out
🏈Best 1-on-1 recovery rep from rookie OT Enrique Cruz Jr. so far. Ogbo Okoronkwo beat him off the snap but Cruz did well to readjust. Raw prospect, but some progress is evident

title: Eagles Training Camp Play of the Day, Day 9: Darius Cooper 🚨🚨🚨 FIRST TWO-TIME WINNER ALERT 🚨🚨🚨 Another day, another great practice from Darius Cooper. It is almost becoming reptitive to say, but that doesn’t make it any less impressive — each and every practice Cooper makes a play that stands out. On Monday there were two noteworthy catches from Cooper, who has six catches from Jalen Hurts and eight targets overall. The first impressive catch from Cooper was along the sideline. Cooper’s body was facing the field as he ran but when the throw came he had to adjust to where it was, as Hurts threw it away from danger and where only Cooper could get it. In order to get it, however, Cooper had to turn his body while running — which he was able to do and held on for the catch. It was extremely impressive body control by Cooper and great hands to hold on. The second impressive catch was what is becoming a regular occurrence from Cooper. The ball came to Cooper over the middle on a crossing route in tight coverage but Cooper held on, using his strong hands to control the ball all the way to the ground and make the catch. At this point it feels like, especially with Devonta Smith out, Cooper is the player Hurts goes to when he needs a catch or doesn’t have anywhere else to go with the ball. Cooper is much, much closer to WR2 than he is WR4 at this point. He also might be the favorite at this point to win ESP’s 2026 Player of Training Camp Award.

Eagles Training Camp Play of the Day, Day 9: Darius Cooper

🚨🚨🚨 FIRST TWO-TIME WINNER ALERT 🚨🚨🚨

Another day, another great practice from Darius Cooper. 

It is almost becoming reptitive to say, but that doesn’t make it any less impressive — each and every practice Cooper makes a play that stands out. 

On Monday there were two noteworthy catches from Cooper, who has six catches from Jalen Hurts and eight targets overall. 

The first impressive catch from Cooper was along the sideline. Cooper’s body was facing the field as he ran but when the throw came he had to adjust to where it was, as Hurts threw it away from danger and where only Cooper could get it. In order to get it, however, Cooper had to turn his body while running — which he was able to do and held on for the catch. It was extremely impressive body control by Cooper and great hands to hold on. 

The second impressive catch was what is becoming a regular occurrence from Cooper. The ball came to Cooper over the middle on a crossing route in tight coverage but Cooper held on, using his strong hands to control the ball all the way to the ground and make the catch. 

At this point it feels like, especially with Devonta Smith out, Cooper is the player Hurts goes to when he needs a catch or doesn’t have anywhere else to go with the ball. 

Cooper is much, much closer to WR2 than he is WR4 at this point. He also might be the favorite at this point to win ESP’s 2026 Player of Training Camp Award.
